# Cade Mini

> A small, durable coding agent built on one append-only session log.

# Cade Mini

<!-- source: README.md -->

# Cade Mini

Cade Mini is the small coding agent in the Cade repository. It keeps one rule at
the center of the design:

> The session log is the source of truth. The model-visible history is a
> deterministic projection. Request construction only produces the current
> request.

The result is a small agent that can survive compaction, window changes, and
process restarts without inventing history.

## Start here

- [Quickstart](quickstart.md) installs and runs the first task.
- [CLI](cli.md) lists one-shot, REPL, session, web, and recovery commands.
- [Configuration](configuration.md) documents `cade-mini.json`.
- [Architecture](architecture.md) explains the log, projection, request, and run
  pipeline.
- [Sessions and context](sessions-context.md) covers resume, compaction,
  pruning, and history retrieval.
- [Tools and security](tools-security.md) covers modes, rules, grants, shell
  analysis, and the sandbox.
- [Snapshots and goals](snapshots-goals.md) covers undo and durable objectives.
- [Skills and memory](skills-memory.md) covers `SKILL.md` and `MEMORY.md`.
- [Hooks, MCP, and subagents](hooks-mcp-subagents.md) covers extensions.
- [Hosts](hosts.md) covers the CLI REPL and the local web host.
- [Development](development.md) covers checks, tests, and the docs pipeline.
- [Parity](parity.md) links the acceptance against Cade.

## Design and reference

The guides are task-oriented. The detailed design and schema references remain
the source of truth for invariants:

- [Cade Mini design](../cade-mini.md)
- [Session log schema](../cade-mini-schema.md)
- [Harvest notes](../cade-mini-harvest.md)
- [Parity acceptance](../cade-mini-parity.md)

## Built docs

The docs are Markdown-first. A small tool validates links and anchors, builds a
single-page site, and generates an `llms.txt` catalog for agents:

```bash
python -m cade.mini.docs check
python -m cade.mini.docs build
```

The generated site is [docs/mini/index.html](../mini/index.html); the generated
catalogs are `docs/cade-mini/llms.txt` and `docs/cade-mini/llms-full.txt`.

# Quickstart

<!-- source: quickstart.md -->

# Quickstart

Cade Mini requires Python 3.12 or newer. The repository uses `uv` for
development and for the `cade-mini` entry point.

## Install and authenticate

From the repository root:

```bash
uv sync --locked
```

Cade Mini reuses Cade's credential store. Configure a provider once with the
Cade login command, or set the provider's API key environment variable:

```bash
cade login
# or
export DEEPSEEK_API_KEY=...
```

Codex uses the stored Codex OAuth credential. `--provider codex` selects it; no
separate Mini login command exists.

## Run one task

```bash
uv run --locked cade-mini "Read README.md and explain the entry point in three bullets."
```

The same command can be written explicitly:

```bash
uv run --locked cade-mini exec "Read README.md and explain the entry point."
```

Cade Mini runs in the current directory by default. Use `--project-root` to
point at another workspace.

## Choose a mode

- `act` is the default. Reads run directly; writes and shell commands ask.
- `build` allows structured writes and read-only shell commands. Mutating shell
  commands still ask.
- `plan` hides write and edit tools and denies mutations. Read-only shell
  commands are allowed.

```bash
uv run --locked cade-mini --mode plan "Propose a fix for the failing test."
uv run --locked cade-mini --mode build "Fix the bug and run the test."
```

For non-interactive automation, `--yes` approves asks, and `--read-only` denies
writes and shell commands. Prefer rule-based allows over `--yes` for shared
repositories; see [Configuration](configuration.md).

## Continue work

Sessions live under `.cade-mini/sessions` by default.

```bash
uv run --locked cade-mini --list-sessions
uv run --locked cade-mini --continue "What did you change?"
uv run --locked cade-mini --resume SESSION_ID "Continue the task."
```

Omitting the task starts the interactive REPL. See [CLI](cli.md) for all REPL
commands.

## Open the web host

```bash
uv run --locked cade-mini --web --port 8765
```

Open `http://127.0.0.1:8765`. The web host has no terminal prompt, so writes and
shell commands are denied unless you start it with `--yes` or use rules. The
host serves one durable session for its lifetime.

## Build the docs

```bash
uv sync --locked --extra docs
uv run --locked python -m cade.mini.docs check
uv run --locked python -m cade.mini.docs build
```

Open `docs/mini/index.html`. The docs source is under `docs/cade-mini/`.

# CLI

<!-- source: cli.md -->

# CLI

The `cade-mini` entry point runs one task, starts a REPL, manages sessions, or
serves the web host.

```bash
cade-mini [TASK] [options]
cade-mini exec TASK [options]
```

`exec` is an explicit alias for a one-shot task. Without a task, `cade-mini`
starts the interactive REPL.

## One-shot options

- `--project-root PATH` sets the workspace. The default is the current
  directory.
- `--config PATH` selects a config file. The default is
  `<project-root>/cade-mini.json`.
- `--provider NAME`, `--model NAME`, and `--effort EFFORT` override provider
  defaults.
- `--mode plan|build|act` selects the execution mode.
- `--read-only` / `--no-read-only` denies or permits writes and shell commands.
- `--yes` approves asks. Use it only in trusted, non-interactive contexts.
- `--auto-review` / `--no-auto-review` lets the model review ask-level calls.
- `--max-steps N` bounds model steps.
- `--context-window N` overrides the model context window.
- `--sandbox off|workspace|strict` selects the Linux bubblewrap policy.
- `--json` emits JSONL events for a one-shot task.

## Sessions

- `--list-sessions` prints ID, update time, and title, then exits.
- `--continue` resumes the latest session in the project.
- `--resume` resumes the latest session; `--resume ID` resumes a specific one.
- `--sessions-dir PATH` changes the session directory. A relative path is
  resolved against the project root.
- `--undo` restores the latest file snapshot and exits without contacting a
  provider.

`--continue` and `--resume` cannot be combined.

## Goals and web host

- `--goal TEXT` sets the workspace goal before running.
- `--web` starts the local web host instead of the REPL.
- `--host` and `--port` bind the web host. The default is `127.0.0.1:8765`.

## REPL commands

- `/new` starts a new session.
- `/resume [ID]` resumes the latest or a specific session.
- `/compact` summarizes older turns.
- `/new-context [NOTE]` starts a new window, optionally with a handoff note.
- `/mode [MODE]` shows or switches the execution mode.
- `/permissions [clear]` shows or clears session grants.
- `/undo` restores the latest snapshot.
- `/goal [TEXT|done|clear]` shows, sets, completes, or clears the goal.
- `/context` prints the session ID, provider, budget, and event count.
- `/help` prints the command list.
- `/exit` or `/quit` exits.

## Exit codes

- `0`: the run completed.
- `1`: the run ended without completion, or no snapshot was available for
  `--undo`.
- `2`: argument, configuration, or startup error.

## Examples

```bash
cade-mini --list-sessions
cade-mini --continue "Summarize the current state."
cade-mini --undo
cade-mini --mode plan "Find the smallest fix for the failing test."
cade-mini --mode build --yes "Fix the test and run pytest."
cade-mini --web --port 8765
```

# Configuration

<!-- source: configuration.md -->

# Configuration

Cade Mini reads `<project-root>/cade-mini.json` by default. Use `--config PATH`
to select another file. Command-line options override the file; the file
overrides built-in defaults.

The file is strict: unknown keys and invalid values are rejected instead of
silently ignored.

## Example

```json
{
  "provider": "deepseek",
  "model": "deepseek-chat",
  "reasoning_effort": "high",
  "context_window": 128000,
  "max_steps": 30,
  "sessions_dir": ".cade-mini/sessions",
  "mode": "act",
  "read_only": false,
  "instructions": true,
  "note": true,
  "memory": true,
  "auto_review": false,
  "prompt_modules": ["identity", "tool_discipline", "working_note", "environment"],
  "sandbox": "workspace",
  "rules": [
    {
      "tool": "bash",
      "command_prefix": "git status",
      "decision": "allow"
    }
  ]
}
```

## Fields

- `provider`, `model`: provider name and model identifier. The CLI flags
  override both.
- `reasoning_effort`: provider reasoning effort. The CLI flag is `--effort`.
- `context_window`: model context window in tokens.
- `max_steps`: maximum model steps in one run.
- `sessions_dir`: session directory. Relative paths resolve against the project
  root.
- `mode`: `plan`, `build`, or `act`.
- `read_only`: deny writes and shell commands.
- `instructions`: load `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md` into request context.
- `note`: load `NOTE.md` working state.
- `memory`: load `MEMORY.md` durable facts.
- `auto_review`: let the model review ask-level tool calls. Default is false.
- `prompt_modules`: system prompt modules. Available names are `identity`,
  `tool_discipline`, `working_note`, and `environment`.
- `sandbox`: `off`, `workspace`, or `strict`. The OS sandbox is implemented on
  Linux with bubblewrap; other hosts keep path, mode, shell, and approval
  checks.

## Rules

Rules are evaluated last match first. A rule matches a tool name or `*`, and
optionally a path or command prefix. `decision` is `allow`, `deny`, or `ask`.

```json
{
  "rules": [
    {"tool": "bash", "command_prefix": "git", "decision": "deny"},
    {"tool": "bash", "command_prefix": "git status", "decision": "allow"},
    {"tool": "write", "path_prefix": "docs/", "decision": "allow"}
  ]
}
```

Hard boundaries win over rules: a path outside the workspace is denied even if a
rule allows the tool. `read_only` also wins over grants and rules.

## Hooks

Hooks run shell commands around tools. A non-zero `before_tool` hook denies the
call.

```json
{
  "hooks": [
    {
      "event": "before_tool",
      "command": "python tools/check_tool.py",
      "matcher": "bash",
      "timeout_ms": 10000
    }
  ]
}
```

`event` is `before_tool` or `after_tool`. `matcher` is a tool name, a prefix
ending in `*`, or omitted for all tools. Hooks receive `CADE_HOOK_EVENT`,
`CADE_TOOL_NAME`, `CADE_TOOL_ARGS`, and `CADE_TOOL_RESULT` in the environment.

## MCP servers

MCP servers use stdio and keep one persistent connection per server.

```json
{
  "mcp_servers": {
    "files": {
      "command": "python",
      "args": ["mcp_server.py"],
      "cwd": ".",
      "timeout_ms": 30000,
      "env": {"LOG_LEVEL": "warn"}
    }
  }
}
```

Discovered tools are exposed as `mcp__<server>__<tool>`. They ask by default,
are denied in plan mode and read-only mode, and can be allowed by a rule.

# Architecture

<!-- source: architecture.md -->

# Architecture

Cade Mini is a pipeline with four stages. Each stage has one owner and one
direction of data flow.

```text
Session log -> Conversation projection -> Request -> Run
```

## Session log

`SessionLog` is an append-only JSONL file. Each entry has an ID, timestamp,
type, parent ID, and data. The active branch ends at the latest entry. A tree is
possible, but the loop follows one branch.

The log stores facts:

- `system`, `user`, `assistant`, and `tool_result` are model-visible facts.
- `compaction` records a summary and `first_kept_id`.
- `window` records a new context start and an optional handoff.
- `request`, `run`, and `attempt` are audit facts. They never become
  conversation messages.

The schema is closed and versioned. See [Session log schema](../cade-mini-schema.md).

## Projection

`project(entries)` is a pure function. It reads the branch and produces the
deterministic conversation projection:

1. Take the latest system message.
2. Apply the latest window start.
3. Apply the latest compaction summary.
4. Keep retained user, assistant, and tool-result messages.
5. Pair tool calls with tool results; insert a synthetic interrupted result at
   the tail when the log ends mid-call.

No projection step writes to the log. Replaying the same entries always
produces the same conversation.

## Request

`build(conversation, tools, budget, context)` admits messages into the current
model window. It:

- joins request-only context such as instructions, skill catalog, NOTE, memory,
  and goal;
- replaces old tool bodies with references to the history tool;
- drops the oldest turns when needed;
- converts the result to provider wire format;
- returns a `Request` with a `BuildReport`.

Admission does not mutate the conversation and does not write facts. A request
that still exceeds the budget is rejected rather than silently truncated.

## Run

`run()` appends the user fact, calls the provider, appends assistant and
tool-result facts, and executes tools. It is the only stage that writes during a
turn. Compaction and window fallback are decisions expressed as new log facts.

## Package map

- `types.py`: log, message, block, and error types.
- `log.py`: append, lock, tail repair, session listing.
- `projection.py`: deterministic conversation projection.
- `request.py`: budget, admission, wire conversion.
- `loop.py`: provider stream, tool execution, retries, facts.
- `compaction.py` and `window.py`: context reduction decisions.
- `tools.py`, `policy.py`, `shell.py`, `sandbox.py`: workspace tools and safety.
- `skills.py`, `memory.py`, `note.py`, `instructions.py`, `goal.py`: request
  context and durable state.
- `hooks.py`, `mcp.py`, `subagents.py`: extension mechanisms.
- `snapshots.py`, `approval.py`, `review.py`: recovery and approvals.
- `cli.py`, `web.py`, `docs.py`: hosts and documentation.

The Mini package imports only `cade.ai` and
`cade.harness.execution_env` from the rest of Cade. It does not import the Cade
agent, product, or server layers. `test_mini_boundary.py` enforces this firewall.

## Why the split

The split prevents a common failure: the request builder starts hiding
messages, then the history rewrite becomes the only copy of what happened. Mini
keeps the original facts and lets the projection and admission be replaced
without losing history.

# Sessions and context

<!-- source: sessions-context.md -->

# Sessions and context

A session is an append-only JSONL file under `.cade-mini/sessions` by default.
The file name is `session-<id>.jsonl`. The session title is derived from the
first user message; no extra event type is needed.

## Resume

```bash
cade-mini --list-sessions
cade-mini --continue "Continue where we stopped."
cade-mini --resume SESSION_ID "Explain the current state."
```

`--continue` and `--resume` open the latest or a specific session. Existing
sessions keep their original system fact; a new `cade-mini.json` does not rewrite
history. If a resumed session has no system entry, the current prompt is added.

## Compaction

When the full conversation exceeds the input budget, `Compactor`:

1. Selects a cut at a visible user boundary.
2. Sends the older messages to the provider for a summary.
3. Appends a `compaction` fact with the summary and `first_kept_id`.
4. Reprojects the conversation as the latest system, summary, and retained tail.

Compaction is iterative: a prior summary is serialized as `PRIOR SUMMARY` and
can be summarized again. The original user, assistant, and tool-result facts
remain in the log.

## Pruning

Request admission replaces old tool results with a reference:

```text
[tool output omitted; call_id=...; use the history tool ...]
```

The latest four tool results are protected first. If the request still does not
fit, older protected results and finally the newest result can be replaced. The
model can recover exact content with the `history` tool using `call_id` or
`entry_id`.

## Windows

A `window` fact starts a new context at a user entry and may include a handoff.
The CLI can start one explicitly with `/new-context`. If compaction cannot bring
a request under budget, the loop can append an automatic window with a fixed
handoff that points to `NOTE.md` and the history tool.

## History tool

`history` accepts one of:

- `query`: case-insensitive search over the branch, returning entry IDs and
  snippets.
- `entry_id`: exact content of one log entry.
- `call_id`: exact tool result for one call.

Exact content is capped. Search results are capped and point back to entry IDs.

## Request context order

For each task the request contains:

1. The system message.
2. Project instructions from `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, or their variants.
3. The skill catalog.
4. `NOTE.md` working state.
5. `MEMORY.md` durable facts.
6. An active goal.

Items 2-6 are request-only context. They are recorded in the request audit but
never become conversation facts. See [Architecture](architecture.md) and the
[design](../cade-mini.md).

# Tools and security

<!-- source: tools-security.md -->

# Tools and security

## Workspace tools

- `read`: read a UTF-8 file with line numbers. Files are capped.
- `write`: write UTF-8 text and create parent directories.
- `edit`: replace one exact occurrence of old text.
- `glob`: list files matching a workspace glob.
- `grep`: search file contents with a regular expression.
- `bash`: run a shell command in the workspace.

## Context and extension tools

- `history`: retrieve compacted or pruned evidence.
- `skill`: load the full body of an available `SKILL.md`.
- `memory`: append a durable fact to `MEMORY.md`.
- `goal`: read, set, complete, or clear the workspace goal.
- `subagent`: run one child task in its own session.
- `mcp__<server>__<tool>`: tools discovered from a configured MCP server.

## Modes

`plan` exposes read, glob, grep, history, skill, and bash. Writes and edits are
hidden and denied. Only classified read-only shell commands are allowed.

`build` exposes all tools. Writes and edits are allowed. Read-only shell
commands are allowed; mutating or unknown commands ask.

`act` exposes all tools. Writes, edits, and shell commands ask.

`--read-only` denies writes, edits, shell commands, memory, and MCP regardless of
mode. It does not block reads, search, history, skills, or goal state.

## Rules and grants

Static rules live in `cade-mini.json`. They are evaluated last match first and
can match tool, path prefix, and command prefix. A hard path boundary always
wins.

A session grant is created when an approval answer is `a` (always). The grant
matches the same tool and the same path or command. `/permissions` lists grants;
`/permissions clear` removes them. Grants last for the process only. Use rules
for durable policy.

## Shell classification

The shell analyzer labels a command as `read_only`, `mutating`, or `unknown`.
It is deliberately conservative:

- `ls`, `cat`, `grep`, `rg`, `git status`, `git diff`, and similar commands are
  read-only.
- `rm`, `mv`, `cp`, `git commit`, `python`, and other mutating commands are
  mutating.
- Pipelines, redirections, command lists, substitutions, and unknown binaries
  are unknown.

Plan mode denies unknown commands. Build and act ask.

## Approvals

An ask is answered by:

- `--yes`: approve.
- `--auto-review`: ask the model for `ALLOW` or `DENY`; failures deny.
- Otherwise a TTY prompt: `y` once, `n` deny, `a` always for this exact call.
- Non-TTY without `--yes` or auto-review: deny.

## Sandbox

On Linux, `--sandbox workspace` or `--sandbox strict` wraps shell commands with
bubblewrap. The sandbox confines the workspace and denies network access by
default. On other hosts the sandbox is unavailable and Cade Mini keeps path
boundaries, mode policy, shell classification, and approvals.

## Best practices

- Use `plan` for review and `build` for scoped edits.
- Prefer explicit rules over `--yes` in shared repositories.
- Keep commands simple so the classifier can reason about them.
- Use `--read-only` for inspection-only automation.

# Snapshots and goals

<!-- source: snapshots-goals.md -->

# Snapshots and goals

## File snapshots

Cade Mini records a snapshot before a file tool changes a file. Snapshots live
under `.cade-mini/snapshots` with a JSONL index and one directory per snapshot.

Covered changes:

- `write` and `edit`.
- Common single-command shell mutations: `rm`, `mv`, `cp`, `touch`, `mkdir`,
  redirection with `>`, and `sed -i`.
- Creating a file records that it did not exist; undo removes it.

Not covered:

- Complex pipelines, command lists, unknown scripts, and commands that mutate
  files without naming them.
- Files larger than the snapshot limit (5 MiB) are rejected rather than
  silently skipped.
- Directory trees are not copied; directory mutations are skipped.

## Undo

```bash
cade-mini --undo
```

This restores the latest snapshot and exits without contacting a provider. In
the REPL, use `/undo`. Each call restores one snapshot, so repeated undo walks
back through the recorded changes.

Snapshots are project state, not session facts. They are not part of the
JSONL session branch.

## Goals

A goal is one durable objective stored in `.cade-mini/goal.json`. It has an
objective, a status (`active` or `done`), and an update time.

```bash
cade-mini --goal "Add a regression test for the parser" "Start the task."
```

In the REPL:

- `/goal` shows the current goal.
- `/goal TEXT` sets an active goal.
- `/goal done` marks it complete.
- `/goal clear` removes it.

The `goal` tool provides the same actions to the model. An active goal is added
to request context so a resumed or compacted session still knows the objective.
Goals are host state; they do not change the session schema.

Goals are intentionally small. Use `NOTE.md` for working details and `MEMORY.md`
for facts that outlive the objective.

# Skills and memory

<!-- source: skills-memory.md -->

# Skills and memory

## Skills

Cade Mini discovers `SKILL.md` files in three roots:

1. `~/.cade/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` for user skills.
2. `<project>/.cade/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` for project skills.
3. `<project>/.cade-mini/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` for Mini-specific skills.

Later roots override earlier roots with the same skill name. A skill file can
start with YAML frontmatter:

```markdown
---
name: release-check
description: Validate release metadata before tagging.
---

Run the release checklist...
```

`name` defaults to the parent directory. `description` defaults to the first
non-empty body line. Invalid names and empty bodies are skipped.

The request gets a compact `<available-skills>` catalog with names and
descriptions. The model loads a body on demand with the `skill` tool:

```json
{"name": "release-check"}
```

Skill bodies are facts in the tool result, not request-only context. Loading the
same skill twice is harmless but adds another tool result.

## Memory

`MEMORY.md` at the project root stores durable facts. It is loaded into request
context as `<memory source="MEMORY.md">` on every task, capped at 32 KiB.

The model appends facts with the `memory` tool:

```json
{"text": "Prefer pytest and keep changes minimal."}
```

`memory` writes only `MEMORY.md`; it cannot write arbitrary paths. The file is
capped at 64 KiB for writes. Remove stale entries manually when it fills.

Memory is different from the other state files:

- `AGENTS.md` is project instruction, owned by the project.
- `NOTE.md` is short-lived working state; it is summarized with compaction.
- `MEMORY.md` is a durable preference or convention.
- The session log is the record of what happened.

## Request context

Instructions, skill catalog, `NOTE.md`, `MEMORY.md`, and an active goal are all
request-only context. They appear in each request audit but never become
conversation messages. See [Sessions and context](sessions-context.md).

# Hooks, MCP, and subagents

<!-- source: hooks-mcp-subagents.md -->

# Hooks, MCP, and subagents

## Hooks

Hooks run shell commands around tools. They are configured in `cade-mini.json`:

```json
{
  "hooks": [
    {
      "event": "before_tool",
      "command": "python tools/check_tool.py",
      "matcher": "bash",
      "timeout_ms": 10000
    }
  ]
}
```

- `before_tool` runs after policy and approval, before the tool executes. A
  non-zero exit denies the call and records an error tool result.
- `after_tool` runs after a successful or failed executed tool. Its output is
  ignored.
- `matcher` is an exact tool name, a prefix ending in `*`, or omitted for all.
- Commands run with the workspace as the working directory and receive
  `CADE_HOOK_EVENT`, `CADE_TOOL_NAME`, `CADE_TOOL_ARGS`, and
  `CADE_TOOL_RESULT`.

Hooks are trusted configuration. A hook that hangs is killed after its timeout.

## MCP

MCP servers use stdio. Cade Mini starts one persistent process per server and
discovers its tools at startup:

```json
{
  "mcp_servers": {
    "files": {
      "command": "python",
      "args": ["mcp_server.py"],
      "timeout_ms": 30000
    }
  }
}
```

Tools are named `mcp__<server>__<tool>`. Their input schema comes from the
server's `tools/list` response. Calls run sequentially over the connection and
preserve server state.

Policy:

- `plan` mode hides MCP tools and denies them.
- `read_only` denies them.
- `build` and `act` ask by default; a rule can allow a specific tool.

A server that fails to start is reported at startup and skipped. Connections
are closed at process exit.

## Subagents

The `subagent` tool runs one child task in its own session and returns the final
answer with the child session ID:

```json
{"prompt": "Find the failing test and report the file and line."}
```

The child:

- gets the parent's provider, budget, policy, approver, hooks, and request
  context;
- gets the base tools plus a history tool bound to its own log;
- does not get another `subagent` tool, so it cannot recurse;
- uses at most 20 steps;
- writes its own session under `<sessions>/subagents/`.

The parent records only the tool call and the returned summary. The child log
keeps the detailed evidence.

## Limits

MCP is a small stdio client, not a full capability negotiation implementation.
Hooks are shell commands, not in-process callbacks. Subagents are sequential and
share the parent's approval context rather than running in parallel.

# Hosts

<!-- source: hosts.md -->

# Hosts

Cade Mini has two hosts: the terminal CLI and a local web host. Both use the
same session log, request builder, tools, and policy.

## Terminal

Without a task, the CLI starts a REPL:

```bash
cade-mini
```

The REPL prints tool progress to stderr, streams assistant text to stdout, and
accepts the commands listed in [CLI](cli.md). With a task, it runs once and
exits:

```bash
cade-mini "Fix the failing test."
cade-mini exec "Fix the failing test."
```

One-shot mode supports `--json` for a JSONL event stream. The REPL does not.

## Web

```bash
cade-mini --web --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8765
```

Open `http://127.0.0.1:8765`. The page submits tasks and displays the final
answer.

Endpoints:

- `GET /` serves the page.
- `POST /api/task` accepts `{"task": "..."}` and returns the answer,
  termination, steps, error, and session ID.
- `GET /api/sessions` returns the session list.

The web host serves one session for its lifetime. Requests are serialized so two
browser tabs cannot interleave turns.

Security:

- The server binds to loopback by default.
- There is no terminal to answer an approval prompt. Without `--yes` or a rule,
  writes and shell commands are denied while reads still work.
- `--read-only` denies mutations explicitly.

## Choosing a host

Use the terminal for interactive review and approvals. Use the web host for a
small local console or a demo. Use one-shot mode for scripts and CI, with
`--read-only` or explicit rules rather than a blanket `--yes`.

There is no separate TUI workbench. The REPL provides terminal interaction, and
the web host provides a browser surface.

# Development

<!-- source: development.md -->

# Development

## Setup

```bash
uv sync --locked --extra dev
```

Run checks from the repository root:

```bash
uv run --locked ruff check src/cade/
uv run --locked ruff format --check src/cade/
uv run --locked pyright src/cade/
uv run --locked pytest -q src/cade/tests
```

For Mini-focused work:

```bash
uv run --locked pytest -q \
  src/cade/tests/test_mini_log.py \
  src/cade/tests/test_mini_projection.py \
  src/cade/tests/test_mini_request.py \
  src/cade/tests/test_mini_loop.py \
  src/cade/tests/test_mini_cli.py
```

The full suite includes a few Windows-only failures in unrelated Cade modules;
check the current CI and test summary before treating them as regressions.

## Documentation

The docs source is `docs/cade-mini/`. The manifest is
`docs/cade-mini/docs.json`; it defines navigation order and which pages are
published.

```bash
uv sync --locked --extra docs
uv run --locked python -m cade.mini.docs check
uv run --locked python -m cade.mini.docs build
uv run --locked python -m cade.mini.docs llms --write
```

`check` validates the manifest, page files, relative links, and anchors. The CI
workflow runs it without the docs extra, because checking uses only the standard
library.

`build` renders `docs/mini/index.html` from Markdown and the manifest. It needs
`markdown-it-py`, installed by the `docs` extra.

`llms --write` updates `docs/cade-mini/llms.txt` and
`docs/cade-mini/llms-full.txt`. The first is an agent catalog; the second
contains the full page bodies.

### Adding a page

1. Add the Markdown file under `docs/cade-mini/`.
2. Add it to a section in `docs.json`.
3. Use relative links to other pages.
4. Run `python -m cade.mini.docs check`.
5. Regenerate `llms.txt` and the site.

Every Markdown file under `docs/cade-mini/` must be listed in the manifest,
except paths matching `exclude` (decision records are excluded).

### Writing style

- Use active voice and short sentences.
- Lead with the task, then the details.
- Use fenced code blocks with a language.
- Keep commands copy-pasteable.
- State limitations explicitly.

The repository language rules apply: code comments and docstrings are Chinese;
documentation, prompts, and UI text are English.

## Boundaries

Mini imports only `cade.ai` and `cade.harness.execution_env` from the rest of
Cade. `src/cade/tests/test_mini_boundary.py` enforces the import firewall. Do not
add imports from `cade.coding_agent`, `cade.server`, or the Cade harness session
layers.

Public interfaces include the session schema, config fields, CLI flags, tool
names, and docs manifest. Change them with tests and documentation in the same
commit.

# Parity

<!-- source: parity.md -->

# Parity

Cade Mini was accepted against Cade on two real repository workflows and a
session resume. The full report is [Cade Mini parity](../cade-mini-parity.md).

## Workflows

Two clean Git repositories started from the same baseline and the same
`AGENTS.md` instruction: "Run pytest after changes. Keep changes minimal."

Bug fix:

- Task: fix `add` in `calc.py` so pytest passes.
- Both agents changed `a - b` to `a + b`, ran pytest, got one passing test, and
  answered `FIXED`.

Feature:

- Task: add `mul(a, b)` and a test.
- Both agents produced the same diff, ran pytest, got two passing tests, and
  answered `PASS`.

Resume:

- Both agents resumed their prior session, recalled `calc.py`, and identified
  the corrected `+` operator.

## Evidence

- Mini ran with `--mode build --yes`; Cade ran with `--mode build --approval
  auto-review`.
- Both used DeepSeek `deepseek-chat`.
- Mini used five steps per workflow; Cade used four. Mini issued an extra `glob`
  inspection, which did not change the result.
- Cade emits JSONL telemetry and budget/approval events; Mini emits human tool
  progress and appends request/run facts to its session log.

## Differences

- Mini's snapshots cover write/edit and common single-command shell mutations;
  complex pipelines are not covered.
- Mini's MCP client is persistent per server but has a narrower capability
  surface than Cade's.
- The OS sandbox is Linux-only; Windows keeps path boundaries, modes, shell
  classification, and approvals.
- The live Codex acceptance passed: write created `codex.txt`, and a resumed
  Codex session read it back.

The parity report records the concrete fixtures and observed results. Re-run a
workflow by creating a clean fixture, running both agents with the settings
above, and comparing the diff and test result rather than the prose answer.
